XI.}}</noinclude>foules of the aire. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=7}}† And I heard also a voice saying to me, Arise Peter, kil and eate. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=8}}† And I said, Not so Lord: for common or vncleane thing neuer entred into my mouth. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=9}}† And a voice ansvvered the second time from heauen: That vvhich God hath made cleane, doe not thou call common. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=10}}† And this vvas done thrise: and al vvere taken vp againe into heauen. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=11}}† And behold, three men immediatly vvere come to the house vvherein I vvas, sent to me from Cæsaréa. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=12}}† And the spirit said to me, that I should goe vvith them, doubting nothing. And there came vvith me these sixe brethren also: and vve vvent in to the mans house. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=13}}† And he told vs, hovv he had seen an Angel in his house, standing and saying to him, Send to Ioppé, and cal hither Simon, that is surnamed Peter, {{verse|chapter=11|verse=14}}† vvho shal speake to thee vvordes vvherein thou shalt be saued and al thy house. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=15}}† And vvhen I had begonne to speake, the holy Ghost fel vpon them, as vpon vs also in the beginning. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=16}}† And I remembred the vvord of our Lord, according as he said, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 1, 5.''}}* ''Iohn in deede baptized vvith vvater, but you shal be baptized vvith the holy Ghost''. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=17}}† If therfore God hath giuen them the same grace, as to vs also that beleeued in our Lord {{sc|Iesvs Christ}}: vvho vvas I that might prohibite God? {{verse|chapter=11|verse=18}}† Hauing heard these things, they {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Good Christians heare and obey gladly such truthes as be opened vnto them from God by their cheefe Pastors, by vision, reuelation, or otherwise.}}∷ held their peace: and glorified God, saying, God then to the Gentiles also hath giuen repentance vnto life.

{{verse|chapter=11|verse=19}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 8, 1.''}}* And they truely that had been dispersed by the tribulation that vvas made vnder Steuen, vvalked through out vnto Phœnîce and Cypres & Antioche, speaking the vvord to none, but to the Ievves only. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=20}}† But certaine of them vvere men of Cypres and Cyréne, vvho vvhen they vvere entred into Antioche, spake to the Greekes, preaching our Lord {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=21}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Epistle vpõ S. Barnabees day Iun. 11.}}And the hand of our Lord vvas vvith them: and a great number of beleeuers vvas conuerted to our Lord. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=22}}† And the report came to the eares of the Church that vvas at Hierusalem, touching these things: and they sent {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 4, 36.''}}* Barnabas as farre as Antioche. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=23}}† Vvho vvhen he vvas come, and savv the grace of God, reioyced: and he exhorted al vvith purpose of hart to continew in our Lord: {{verse|chapter=11|verse=24}}† because he vvas a good man, and ful of the holy Ghost and faith. And a great {{sup|‖}} multitude vvas added to our Lord. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=25}}† And he vvent, forth to {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 9, 30.''}}* Tarsus, to seeke Saul: {{verse|chapter=11|verse=26}}† vvhom vvhen he had found, he brought him to Antioche.
